assigned.title: Install, upgrade, uninstall, reinstall — tested, not assumed
assigned.acceptance: The installer's lifecycle is exercised automatically wherever that is possible on a runner, and everything that is not is named for the commander's machine. REQUIRED: clean install on a machine that has never had the application, then launch. REQUIRED: upgrade over a previous version with user data preserved, which is the one a release breaks most often and nobody tests. REQUIRED: uninstall leaves no service, no scheduled task and no orphaned node.exe, and states exactly what user data it keeps or removes. REQUIRED: reinstall after uninstall. REQUIRED: each case is marked automated or commander-machine, with the reason, so the split is visible rather than implied.

recommended.title: The desktop forwarder spec shares one ledger across parallel workers
recommended.acceptance: The desktop forwarder spec gives the same answer however many workers Playwright runs it with. It does not today: the stub backend keeps ONE request ledger for the whole process, three tests clear it and then assert it holds exactly their own request, and playwright.config.ts sets fullyParallel: true -- which splits tests WITHIN a file across workers. A two-core machine gets one worker and the file passes; a CI runner gets several and a neighbour's forwarded request lands between the clear and the read. CI run 37007312900 failed exactly that way on three assertions, and --workers=4 reproduces it locally. REQUIRED: the isolation is structural rather than a matter of how many cores the machine running it happens to have. REQUIRED: toHaveLength(1) survives unchanged -- it is the assertion that a forwarder neither retries nor fans out, which the spec records as 'a duplicated session request against a real backend is a duplicated authorization', and relaxing it to 'at least one' would delete the check in order to make the schedule convenient. REQUIRED: the repair is demonstrated under more workers than the machine has cores, because a pass at one worker is what hid this for as long as it was hidden.
recommended.notes: FILED IN ROUND 104 from CI run 37007312900 on d6d0324, which is the first run after the branch was published. Not caused by that round: neither PW-0309 nor PW-0503 touches this spec, the stub or the forwarder.

recommended.title: The automated half of the Windows matrix, running on Windows
recommended.acceptance: Every row PW-0601 marks automated runs on a windows-latest runner and fails the build when it fails. REQUIRED: the existing e2e suite runs against the DESKTOP target on Windows, not only the web target on Ubuntu -- the desktop axis is currently built on Ubuntu only, and only incidentally, because the axis defaults on and openssl happens to be installed. REQUIRED: the shell is driven end to end where the harness can reach it, and where it cannot, the row stays in the commander-machine half rather than being replaced by a unit test that proves something easier. REQUIRED: retries stay at zero, on the rule playwright.config.ts already states at length. REQUIRED: a row that is skipped says why, by name, the way the existing harness already does for the desktop and media-rig axes.
